_note: Hand-drawn, simplified regions for the map page. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude]. Edges are approximate on purpose; edit freely. 'pattern' must match a pattern id in js/map.js.

properties.name: Golan Heights
properties.description: A high basalt plateau east of the Hula Valley and the Sea of Galilee, built from old lava flows. Dark volcanic soil, open grassland and steep canyons running down to the Jordan.

properties.name: Upper Galilee
properties.description: The highest, wettest hills west of the Jordan, covered in oak, pine and terebinth woodland. Mountain towns like Tzfat sit on ridges above deep valleys.

properties.name: Lower Galilee and Jezreel Valley
properties.description: Rolling hills and broad valleys, with the flat Jezreel Valley as the country's largest farming plain. Kibbutzim and moshavim are spread across a patchwork of fields.

properties.name: Carmel and Coastal Plain
properties.description: A strip of sand, dunes and orchards along the Mediterranean, backed by the Carmel ridge and the low hills of Menashe. Most of the country's population lives here, from Haifa through Tel Aviv-Yafo.

properties.name: Jordan Valley and Sea of Galilee basin
properties.description: Part of the Great Rift, dropping from the Hula Valley through the Sea of Galilee to the Jordan Valley, well below sea level. Hot, fertile and fed by springs, with date groves and fishponds.

properties.name: Judean Hills and Jerusalem
properties.description: Limestone hills about 800 meters high, carved into stone terraces for vines, olives and orchards. Jerusalem sits on the ridge where the hills meet the desert.

properties.name: Judean Desert and Dead Sea
properties.description: Bare hills and canyons in the rain shadow east of the ridge, falling to the Dead Sea, the lowest place on land. Salt flats, cliffs and a few spring-fed oases like Ein Gedi.

properties.name: Northern Negev and Be'er Sheva
properties.description: Semi-arid plains of fine loess soil, green for a few weeks after winter rain and dry the rest of the year. Be'er Sheva is its main city, with farms and planted forests around it.

properties.name: Negev Highlands and Ramon Crater
properties.description: A rocky desert plateau cut by the Ramon Crater, a 40-kilometer erosion cirque with colored sandstone and basalt. Very little rain falls, and the night skies are some of the darkest in the country.

properties.name: Arava and Eilat
properties.description: A long, hot valley of sand and acacia running south from the Dead Sea to the Red Sea at Eilat. Farming here depends on desert agriculture and groundwater.
